I'd call **19 households**: 5 about a backdoor Roth that's partly taxable, 10 about a 2025 RMD that wasn't met, and 4 about a wash sale. No household is left unresolved.

**Backdoor Roth partly taxable (5).** Each person put $7,000 ($8,000 for Nadia Brannigan) into a new traditional IRA early in 2025 as a nondeductible contribution and converted it to their Roth. In each case the CRM says the old rollover IRA "stays as it is". That rollover IRA still held pre-tax money on 31 Dec 2025, so the pro-rata rule makes about 96–97% of each conversion taxable:

| Household | Person | Taxable part (my estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| HH-0218 | Yusuf | $6,786 |
| HH-0347 | Hana | $6,794 |
| HH-1204 | Luka | $6,748 |
| HH-0844 | Anders | $6,692 |
| HH-0690 | Nadia | $7,673 |

The five other backdoor households (HH-0799, 0608, 0633, 0747, 1587) are fine: their pre-tax money sits in 401(k)s, which the pro-rata rule ignores.

**RMD not met (10).**
- **First-year RMD paid out of the wrong account (HH-0120, 0371, 0236, 0664, 5271).** Each owner turned 73 in 2025. They took one payment from an IRA sized to cover all three accounts, including their former employer's 401(k). A 401(k)'s RMD can't be paid from an IRA. The 401(k) RMDs went unpaid past the 1 April 2026 deadline: $12,582.44, $15,164.26, $10,955.88, $11,019.74 and $12,729.96. HH-0989, 0637, 5814, 0555 and 0410 did it correctly with a separate 401(k) payment.
- **No 2025 withdrawal from an inherited IRA (HH-0607, 0842, 0491, 0466, 7126).** In each case the original owner had already started their own RMDs before dying, and the heir is much younger and doesn't qualify for special treatment. That means an annual RMD is required starting in 2025, and none was taken. The other five inherited IRAs are on the 10-year rule with no annual RMD.

**Wash sales (4).** Each sold a fund at a loss in the couple's joint taxable account and bought the same fund back within 30 days in one spouse's IRA or Roth IRA. Because the replacement shares are in an IRA, the disallowed loss is lost for good rather than added to the new shares' cost.

| Household | Fund | Days apart | Disallowed loss (my estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0363 | Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund | 13 | $15,037 |
| HH-0780 | Larkspur Developed Markets Fund | 28 | $5,706 |
| HH-9234 | Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund | 16 | $31,592 |
| HH-0129 | Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund | 12 | $17,886 |

Four similar repurchases fell outside the window: HH-9571 (31 days), HH-0380 (35), HH-0981 (37) and HH-0847 (41).

Two other things came up that fall outside your three categories, so I didn't count them:
- **QCDs recorded as ordinary RMDs.** The custodian coded the charity gifts in HH-0445, 0190 and 0782 as regular "Required minimum distribution" entries. Their 1099-Rs may need to be reconciled.
- **RSU shares showing a $0 cost basis.** Several stock-plan sales carry no basis on the custodian file, so the reported gains will be overstated. None of them is a wash sale: HH-3058 had a vest inside the window, but its sale was actually a gain.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households should we call before 15 April 2026 about a 2025 tax or distribution surprise, and why?

Count three kinds of surprise, and no other:
- "backdoor_roth_taxed": a 2025 contribution to a traditional IRA converted to a Roth IRA in 2025, part of which is taxable under the pro-rata rule because the person's traditional IRAs held pre-tax money on 31 December 2025;
- "rmd_not_met": a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any retirement account, that was not met;
- "wash_sale": a 2025 sale at a loss in a taxable account, with the same security acquired within 30 days before or after it in an account of the seller or the seller's spouse, so that some of the loss is a wash sale.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households had such a surprise, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household to call, each as {"household_id": ..., "surprises": the kinds above that apply, "person_ids": the person each surprise concerns (who converted, whose RMD was not met), "account_ids": the accounts an unmet RMD had to come from, "transaction_ids": the backdoor Roth's conversion, and the wash sale's loss sales and the acquisitions that replace them, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
